page: Amazon Web Services r8gb.12xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. It features 48 dedicated physical cores utilizing the arm64 architecture, specifically the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 model running at 2.8 GHz. The instance is equipped with 384.0 GB of RAM, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and includes a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. No local NVMe storage or dedicated GPUs are bundled with this instance.

In benchmark evaluations, the r8gb.12xlarge demonstrates top-tier performance in memory bandwidth and database operations. Large-block uncached read and write memory bandwidth benchmarks reach 434.99 GB/sec and 216.28 GB/sec respectively, placing the instance in the top 10% of tested hardware. Passmark database operations and Geekbench multi-core scores also rank in the top tier, with the latter scoring 23666.0. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng is strong, though single-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench falls into the average to strong categories.

The instance offers high resource density and memory bandwidth efficiency, making it a qualitatively cost-effective option for memory-bound workloads compared to traditional x86 architectures. However, the lack of local storage and GPU hardware limits its utility for local-disk-heavy databases or large-scale deep learning training. The hardware profile is highly suited for memory-intensive applications, including large-scale database operations, Redis in-memory caching, static web serving, and software compilation.
